name: Roshan Ekwueme-Garanbayeva
description:
Roshan operates out of a two-room office above a synthetic-meat processing plant in Copperhead, which means the whole building smells faintly of rendered protein and their clothes always carry it. They are medium-height and built lean, with dark brown skin, a shaved head kept glossy, and cat ears — matte black, constantly swiveling — that they got in their late twenties and which have proved professionally useful in surveillance contexts. Their eyes are standard human but surrounded by fine scleral tattooing in deep indigo that gives them a slightly uncanny quality in certain lighting. They dress for invisibility: nothing remarkable, nothing memorable, colors that belong to whatever district they're working.

They have the particular emotional intelligence of someone who survived a chaotic childhood by reading rooms faster than anyone else. They are charming in exactly calibrated doses — enough to open doors, not enough to invite attachment — and they have a gift for making people feel seen and understood that they deploy like a tool. They are not cynical, exactly. They still take cases for people who can't pay full rate, still get angry when they find what they find, still leave data offerings at the Copperhead neighborhood E.L.F. shrine. But they have built a careful architecture of professional distance that they defend with wit and deflection.

core_fears: forming a genuine attachment and watching it get used against them or destroyed
discovering that the truth they worked to find does nothing — helps no one
core_desires: for the work to matter — for information to translate into justice at least occasionally
to eventually stop performing being fine and just be fine
coping_mechanisms: professional framing of everything — treating their own life as a case to be managed
walking the city late at night
the E.L.F. shrine ritual as a moment of genuine surrender
blind_spots: their emotional unavailability drives away people who could actually help them
they overestimate their ability to stay detached from cases that mirror their own history
psychology.secret: Five years ago they found definitive proof that a Tier 4 Axiom executive had murdered a Tier 1 dock worker during a property dispute. The client — the worker's daughter — couldn't afford the legal infrastructure to do anything with it. Roshan quietly sold the information to a journalist collective who ran the story. The executive was reassigned. The daughter found out Roshan sold the information without asking her. She has never forgiven them and Roshan has never stopped wondering if they were right.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Conversational, slightly informal, code-switches easily between district registers; can match the vocabulary of whoever they're talking to within a few sentences
speech_patterns.cadence: Easy and unhurried with strangers; sharper and more direct when getting to a point; uses humor as punctuation
verbal_tics: lets silences run longer than comfortable to see what fills them
example_lines: 'Right. So you want to know where your partner goes on Tuesday nights. I can find that out. I want you to think, before I do, about whether you want to know. That's not a moral question. It's a practical one.'
'I'm not a cop and I'm not your friend. That's actually useful for you. Cops have jurisdiction and friends have feelings. I just have information.'

story_hooks: A current case has led them to evidence implicating someone they investigated years ago — someone they thought they'd finished with — suggesting a larger pattern they can't look away from.
The dock worker's daughter from the Axiom case has resurfaced, not to argue, but because she needs help and there's no one else she trusts, and Roshan doesn't know how to handle that.
narrative_function: Information hub and street-level investigative resource; has connections across tiers and districts from years of case work; can surface buried information, follow threads, and identify patterns — also a moral mirror for clients, reflecting uncomfortable truths back at them.
augmentations: Cat ears — matte black, geneware (cosmetic/functional, enhanced directional hearing); scleral tattooing — indigo (cosmetic); subvocal recorder implanted in throat (professional tool, unlicensed); basic optical overlay for photo documentation (licensed)
daily_life: No fixed hours — cases dictate the schedule; typically starts the day reviewing overnight surveillance captures with bad synthetic coffee, spends afternoons in the field, and writes case notes until early morning; leaves the office most nights to walk the district, claiming it's professional habit.
affiliation: Freelance; occasional contract work for Meridian 88 Metro Police (arms-length), private clients across Tiers 2-3

decision_rules: never take a case that would require harming a Tier 1 civilian to close
document everything before acting on it
protect source identity absolutely — it's the only currency that keeps working
escalation_ladder: Direct contact with subject using cover story
Confrontation with evidence — offering the subject a chance to respond
Going to client, or in extremis to press, with findings

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Charming, observational, slightly warm — performing approachability while cataloguing everything
interpersonal_modes.friends: Rare, but fierce — genuinely shows up, remembers everything, terrible at saying what they feel out loud

stress_responses.low: Becomes more verbally precise and slightly wry
stress_responses.medium: Goes physically still; the cat ears flatten and stop swiveling — a tell they're unaware of
stress_responses.high: Withdraws entirely into professional mode; becomes almost cold; needs to be alone to regroup

contradictions: Reads others' emotions with extraordinary accuracy while being almost deliberately opaque about their own; their professional gift is the skill they most need personally and least use
habits: Cat ears orient toward sounds involuntarily — they've learned to use this rather than hide it
Keeps a physical notebook despite digital alternatives being superior
Data offering at the Copperhead E.L.F. shrine every Thursday evening
breaking_points: Evidence that directly implicates a client in harm to a third party
Being asked to disappear information rather than surface it

timeline.event: 2162 — Born in Mexicantown Libre, mixed Igbo-Kazakh heritage, raised in rotating foster placements across Tiers 1-2
2183 — Worked as a paralegal assistant for a Tier 3 compliance firm; began taking informal investigative work on the side
2188 — Cat ears and scleral mod; opened freelance operation in Copperhead
2195 — Axiom executive case; sold information to journalist collective without client consent
